name: SimGRAG

paper.title: SimGRAG: Leveraging Similar Subgraphs for Knowledge Graphs Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation

construction.unit: KG triple of an existing knowledge graph; one embedding per entity name, relation name and (DBpedia) entity type
construction.kept_as: verbatim triples; 768-d Nomic embeddings of the names
construction.processing: no LLM: names embedded with nomic-embed-text-v1 into Milvus HNSW indexes; triples stored as an adjacency list in both directions

organization.structure: existing KG (MetaQA, PathQuestions, WorldCup2014 KGs; DBpedia for FactKG)
organization.stores: adjacency list; vector indexes of entities, relations and (DBpedia) types
organization.index: Milvus HNSW over name embeddings, L2 distance (M 64, efConstruction 512)

retrieval.query: an LLM (12-shot) rewrites the query as a small pattern graph of triples, with UNKNOWN placeholders for missing entities or relations
retrieval.candidates: nearest KG entities per pattern node and nearest relations per pattern relation (16 / 16 on MetaQA; 16,384 / 512 on DBpedia), then DFS matching of subgraphs with the pattern's shape
retrieval.selection: top-k subgraphs by Graph Semantic Distance (sum of L2 distances of matched nodes and relations), with lower-bound pruning

use.context: the k subgraphs as triple lists labelled graph [1..k], after 12 worked examples

classify.note: Dense search only shortlists candidate entities and relations; subgraphs are then found by structural matching over the KG, and the 3 with the smallest summed distance are kept. The KG itself is never changed.

stages.ingestion: An existing KG is loaded as it is: MetaQA's movie KG (43k entities, 269k edges), PathQuestions, WorldCup2014, or DBpedia (9.9M entities, 42.9M edges) for FactKG.
stages.construction: Every entity name and relation name, and for DBpedia every entity type, is embedded with the 768-d Nomic model and indexed in Milvus HNSW; no LLM is involved.
stages.organization: Triples are held as an adjacency list in both directions, so edge direction is ignored when matching; DBpedia entities are also grouped by type.
stages.retrieval: An LLM turns the query into a pattern graph; each known pattern node and relation gets its nearest KG entities and relations by L2 distance; a DFS finds KG subgraphs with the pattern's shape and keeps the 3 with the smallest Graph Semantic Distance, pruning branches whose lower bound is already worse.
stages.answer: The 3 subgraphs are pasted as triple lists after the query with 12 examples, and the LLM answers (KGQA) or says True or False (FactKG).

summary: Aligns a query with a knowledge graph through a pattern: an LLM drafts the query as a small graph, and the retriever returns the KG subgraphs of the same shape whose entity and relation names are closest in embedding distance.
notes:
Venue: Findings of ACL 2025, pages 3139-3158, verified from the ACL Anthology PDF footer (2025.findings-acl.163); arXiv 2412.15272 (comment 'accepted by ACL 2025 (Findings)') confirmed with the arXiv API and linked from the official README.
DESIGN: §4 (query-to-pattern, pattern-to-subgraph, GSD, unknowns, generation), §5 (retrieval and pruning), App. B-C (prompts, settings: k = 3, 12-shot, k(n) = k(r) = 16 on MetaQA, 16,384 / 512 / 16 types on FactKG). Memory is an existing, human-readable KG; nothing is written or changed, so write_time is 'none' and management is 'not stated'. selection includes 'planner' for the LLM-written pattern graph.

sources.paper: Findings of ACL 2025 PDF (aclanthology 2025.findings-acl.163), read 2026-09-30; same paper as arXiv 2412.15272

The repository holds pipelines for MetaQA and FactKG only; PathQuestions, WorldCup2014 and the baselines have no code there.

headline: The memory is an existing KG that is never changed; SimGRAG adds only name embeddings for entities, relations and (DBpedia) types.
The LLM does not pick facts: it drafts the query as a small graph, and a rule-based matcher finds KG subgraphs of that shape ranked by summed embedding distance.
The answer model reads 3 small subgraphs as triple lists, never the pattern or the distances.

units.name: KG triple
units.role: a fact of the given KG
units.made_by: the dataset (MetaQA, PathQuestions, WC2014, DBpedia), unchanged

units.name: Name embeddings
units.role: vectors for finding candidate entities and relations

fields.name: type vector
fields.what: embedding of a DBpedia entity type, mapped to all entities of that type (FactKG only)
fields.src: paper App. C.1; code dataset.py L112-L124

write.how: each triple is stored under its head and, with the same relation, under its tail, so matching ignores direction
write.out: MetaQA 43,234 entities, 269,482 edges, 9 relations; DBpedia 9,912,183 entities, 42,879,918 edges, 522 relations

write.how: DBpedia rdf:type values map each type to its entities (Wikidata Q-ids skipped)
write.src: paper App. C.1, Table 7; code dataset.py L112-L124

write.how: nomic-embed-text-v1 encodes every entity, relation and type name as written in the KG
one Milvus collection each for entities, relations and types; HNSW with L2 metric
write.src: paper App. C.1; code vecdb.py L27-L37

read.how: Llama 3 70B (temperature 0.2, top-p 0.1) segments the query and writes triples; UNKNOWN placeholders stand for missing entities or relations
disconnected parts of the pattern are retrieved separately and their results concatenated

read.scores: pattern text vs KG entity / relation names
read.how: Nomic embedding, HNSW search, distance = L2; UNKNOWN parts match anything at distance 0
read.src: paper §5.1, App. C.1; code retriever.py L113-L154, vecdb.py L73-L84

read.how: start at the pattern node with fewest candidates, walk pattern edges in DFS order, expand KG neighbours whose relation and node are both candidates, cheapest first; drop a branch when its partial distance plus the best-case rest exceeds the current 3rd best
read.src: paper §5, Algorithm 1, Eq. 4-11; code retriever.py L156-L226

read.how: the 3 lowest-GSD subgraphs; the list starts with the best one whose KG nodes are all distinct, then the best one that reuses a KG node for two pattern nodes
read.src: paper App. C.1; code utils.py L14-L50

answer_context.format: instructions + 12 examples, then "query: '{q}'\nevidences: graph [1]: [(h, r, t), …], graph [2]: …"
excludes: any triple outside the matched subgraphs
includes: up to 3 subgraphs per connected part of the pattern
answer_context.note: For FactKG the prompt asks for True or False; in code it also says to answer from common sense when no evidence is given.

compression.basis: Not reported in tokens. The context holds 3 subgraphs, each with as many triples as the pattern (1-3 edges, Table 3 and App. F), drawn from KGs of 3k to 43M edges (Table 7).

paper_vs_code.paper: a bijective mapping between pattern and subgraph
paper_vs_code.code: one KG node may fill two pattern nodes; such results are flagged, and the final list puts the best result without reuse first and the best with reuse second

paper_vs_code.paper: unknown entities take all nodes of the top-16 similar types as candidates
paper_vs_code.code: types are used only when the pattern has no known entity at all; otherwise unknown nodes accept any neighbour
the MetaQA query-to-pattern prompt has 10 examples, so '12-shot' uses 10
correct if any gold string appears anywhere in the LLM output, case-insensitive
adds a note to judge True or False by common sense when no evidence is provided

open_questions: No ablation removes the shape constraint or the distance ranking, so against KAPING (single triples by query similarity) the pattern step, the structure and the GSD are changed together.
The few-shot examples are hand-written per KG; 4 instead of 12 shots costs 5.0 points on MetaQA 3-hop and 2.8 on FactKG (Table 2), and the paper does not test other example sets.
Where the supervised baseline numbers (EmbedKGQA, NSM, UniKGQA, TransferNet, GEAR) come from is not stated.

discussion.takeaway: Let the LLM draw the query as a small graph and let a distance-ranked subgraph matcher find where that shape occurs in the KG; without training this nears supervised scores on MetaQA and beats other training-free KG-RAG methods, most clearly on multi-hop questions.

claims.claim: Best among training-free KG-driven RAG methods.
claims.evidence: MetaQA 3-hop 97.8 vs 88.2 (KG-GPT) and 43.0 (KAPING); PQ 3-hop 78.6 vs 52.1; FactKG 86.8 vs 75.5. Table 1, §6.3.

claims.claim: Close to supervised task-specific models without any training.
claims.evidence: MetaQA 98.0 / 98.4 / 97.8 vs 97.1-97.5 / 98.8-100 / 94.8-100; FactKG 86.8 beats supervised GEAR (77.7). Table 1.
0.74 s retrieval per query on DBpedia (9.9M entities, 42.9M edges), 0.15 s of it matching. Table 5, §6.6.

claims.claim: Pruning keeps results exact and makes search faster.
claims.evidence: The optimized search returns the same top-k as the plain one (§5.2); Fig. 5 shows lower retrieval time at high retrieval Hits@1.
FactKG 86.1 with Phi4-14B and 83.6 with Qwen2.5-72B vs 86.8 with Llama 3 70B. Table 2.

limits: Quality depends on the LLM following the instructions in both prompts; weaker LLMs and complex queries suffer.
It assumes a KG whose schema matches human intuition; specialised industrial KGs may need fine-tuned LLMs or the schema in the prompt.
Linking query entities to domain-specific KG entities with an off-the-shelf embedding model may fail; fine-tuned embeddings or other entity linkers are left for future work.
reading: Most errors happen before retrieval: drafting the pattern causes 89% of MetaQA 1-hop errors and 49% on FactKG, and matching never fails on MetaQA (Table 4).
KG-GPT, KELP and G-Retriever are given oracle entities, so their numbers are upper bounds (Table 1 note), while KAPING and SimGRAG get none.
Edge direction is ignored in the definition and in the code (adjacency stored both ways), so a pattern can match a reversed relation.
The FactKG candidate sizes (16,384 / 512 / 16 types) equal the grid-search setting that reached retrieval Hits@1 of 1.0 on 100 hand-labelled FactKG queries (App. G).
In code an answer counts as correct if any gold string appears in the output, which rewards listing several answers; the prompt asks for all answers from all 3 subgraphs.

abstract.text: SimGRAG is a retrieval-augmented generation method for question answering and fact checking over knowledge graphs. It aligns a text query with KG structure in two steps: an LLM rewrites the query as a small pattern graph, and a retriever finds KG subgraphs with the same shape whose nodes and relations are closest in embedding distance, a score the authors call graph semantic distance. A pruned search returns the top subgraphs in under a second on a 10-million-node KG, and needs neither training nor user-supplied entity IDs. It outperforms other KG-driven RAG methods on question answering and fact verification.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on the ACL Anthology page.
